_readme: Known third-party panic sites the fuzz campaign is ALLOWED to close on.
Why this exists: libfuzzer-sys installs a panic hook that calls
abort() BEFORE unwinding, so no in-process containment (catch_unwind)
can keep a third-party panic from killing a campaign target. The
engines are exact-pinned pure-Rust crates with no fixed release
available at registration time; forking all of them is out of scope
The gate stays honest because the campaign script ONLY accepts a
crashing target when the panic's file path is under .cargo/registry
(a dependency, never workspace code) AND the crate+location+message
match an entry below EXACTLY. Any other panic - our code, an
unregistered third-party site, a second site in the same crate -
still fails the campaign. Entries must carry a production-impact
When a fixed upstream release lands, REMOVE the entry and the gate
goes back to hard-failing the site.

entries.production_impact: predict() coefficient math wraps silently in release builds (pure Rust, no UB, no memory unsafety); one damaged packet's audio is garbage, the stream continues
entries.containment: decoder boundary catch_unwind -> typed alac.frame.engine-panic corrupt error (crates/codecs/src/audio/alac/decoder.rs); regression-pinned by codecs::audio::alac::fuzz::tests::campaign_seed_survives
entries.discovered: audit run 44229396612 shard 2 (crash-616f4757); reconfirmed 44245745551 shard 2 (same site, the committed seed itself)

entries.production_impact: debug_assert under fuzz builds; in release the same crafted setup header indexes past the codeword table (index-out-of-bounds panic)
entries.containment: build_engine + decode_block_into catch_unwind -> typed vorbis.engine.init-panic / vorbis.packet.decode-panic corrupt errors (crates/codecs/src/audio/vorbis/decoder.rs); regression-pinned by codecs::audio::vorbis::fuzz::tests::campaign_seed_survives (codebook fixture)

entries.production_impact: LPC FIR filter slice arithmetic (out[i - order..i]) underflows when i < order; wraps in release where the malformed range surfaces as a slice-index panic on the same packet - both contained at the decoder boundary
entries.containment: same decode_into catch_unwind -> typed alac.frame.engine-panic corrupt error (crates/codecs/src/audio/alac/decoder.rs); one damaged packet, the stream continues
entries.discovered: audit run 44251372950 shard 2 (crash on a fresh input; the registry correctly refused to blanket-allowlist the unregistered line)

entries.production_impact: f.seq_hdr.clone().unwrap() on a frame decoded without a sequence header - unwrap is NOT debug-only: a crafted stream aborts the process in release builds too (panic unwinding through rav1d's extern "C" shim aborts at the FFI boundary)
entries.containment: none possible in-process (inside rav1d's extern "C" shim over FFI); the player-level mitigation is the process-level decode isolation already assumed for third-party engines - upstream fix required

entries.production_impact: the ITU-T.35 metadata block decrements payload_size once per trailing bit and once per country-code byte on a size attacker controls; truncated metadata underflows any of the -= 1 sites (observed at :2428 and :2435 on different inputs). In release the subtraction wraps negative and the payload_size <= 0 guard at the block's exit rejects the OBU (log line, no UB) - the OBU is skipped and decode continues
entries.containment: none needed for release (wraps to the guarded branch); registered as a LINE RANGE because the block holds several decrement sites that surface one at a time under fuzzing
entries.discovered: audit run 44245745551 shard 3 (:2435, crash-ddfd3d63) and 44255640718 shard 3 (:2428, separate input)
